long_biography.plain_text:
Coumantaros grew up around two family trades: flour milling on his father's side and shipping through his mother's Nomikos family. Displaced to Argentina during the Second World War, he worked for a grain trader and learned how cargo, ports and milling fit together. After moving to New York, he founded Southern Star Shipping, initially operating wartime dry-cargo ships and tankers. He later commissioned self-discharging bulk carriers and shallow-draft vessels designed for difficult ports and industrial customers.

That supply-chain experience shaped his move into Nigerian industry. Coumantaros established Flour Mills of Nigeria as the country sought foreign investment after independence, then expanded the business beyond wheat milling into consumer foods and agro-allied operations. He remained chairman as the company listed publicly and grew into a major employer. Outside business, he applied the same meticulous preparation to ocean racing, building competitive campaigns, winning the Newport Bermuda Trophy after decades of attempts and supporting sailing programmes and institutions.
